title: When the Provision Burns
premise: Coral Underhill, a wayfinder who maps rivers for hire and keeps every human tie at arm's length, is summoned by a letter from the estranged archaeologist father he buried twenty years ago. The tide has exposed a sea cave on the Cornish coast, and inside it Coral finds his father's final journal: a map to the source of the River Vell, where an artifact called the Provision supposedly grants its keeper command over the valley's water—and the town that depends on it. Racing a land developer's hired crew and accompanied by his father's old expedition family, who adopt him whether he likes it or not, Coral follows the river upstream through flooded mines, drowned chapels, and betrayals. At the source he learns the Provision is real but feeds on whoever holds it, and that his father died refusing to use it; when the developer seizes it and begins strangling the valley, Coral must choose between destroying it—losing his last link to his father—and letting power do what power does. He breaks it, floods the cave, and comes home to the found family waiting downstream.
about_author: Petra Delacroix is a former hydrologist who spent a decade surveying forgotten waterways before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted coastguard station in Cornwall, where the tides still dictate her working hours.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On a survey job in Wales, Coral measures a river's course with obsessive precision, dodging a client's invitation to stay for dinner. A solicitor's letter arrives: his dead father's estate has released a sealed item. He burns it, then digs the ashes out of the grate. Beat: loneliness shown as discipline.

chapters.title: The Tide Keeps No Secrets
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He travels to Cornwall intending only to collect the item and leave. The lowest tide in decades exposes a sea cave beneath the cliffs of Porthvell; locals cross themselves rather than look at it. Inside, Coral finds his father's waterproof journal and a brass instrument wrapped in oilcloth. Beat: grief ambushing him in a place he can't walk away from.

chapters.title: Admission Charged in Blood
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The journal describes the Provision—a relic at the river's source that 'answers to the one who holds it'—and warns that the last keeper drowned rather than surrender it. Coral deciphers half the route before realizing someone else has been in the cave recently: fresh boot prints, cigarette ends. Beat: curiosity curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: The Crew That Wouldn't Disband
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Coral tracks the boot prints to the Salt & Anchor pub, where his father's old expedition team—gruff boatwoman Maren, superstitious diver Teo, and sharp-tongued archivist Ines—still meets every year on the anniversary of the dig that ended. They recognize him instantly. Beat: being known against his will, and secretly liking it.

chapters.title: What the Developer Bought
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. A consortium led by Aldous Crane has bought the whole valley, ostensibly for a reservoir; Ines has seen their surveys, which mark the source itself. She shows Coral a photograph of Crane's site manager—the man whose boots were in the cave. Beat: the stakes widen from personal to communal.

chapters.title: Upstream Rules
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral lays out the route: forty miles upriver through abandoned tin mines and a drowned chapel, following markers his father left. Maren offers her boat; Coral refuses company, then accepts it in the same breath. Beat: the first crack in his self-sufficiency.

chapters.title: Flooded Chapel, Standing Congregation
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. The team navigates the submerged chapel by lantern light; Teo nearly drowns retrieving a marker stone, and Coral hauls him out without thinking. Teo tells him his father once did exactly the same for him. Beat: inherited courage, the found family's liturgy.

chapters.title: Crane's Men on the Water
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Crane's crew overtakes them on the estuary—professional, polite, armed with legal threats and a drone. Maren loses them in the fog she's sailed since girlhood, but they've photographed the journal page Coral was studying. Beat: the race becomes real.

chapters.title: The Journal's Second Voice
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Hidden marginalia reveal his father wasn't working alone: a second hand annotated the map, corrections in a script Coral slowly recognizes as his own teenage handwriting—he helped draw this map at fifteen, then erased the memory when his father chose the dig over him. Beat: rage and guilt braided together.

chapters.title: Mine of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. In the tin mine tunnels the team finds evidence Crane's men came through weeks ago—and one of them, injured and abandoned, still alive. Coral wants to leave him; Ines shames him gently; they carry him out. Beat: mercy as a choice that costs time they don't have.

chapters.title: What the Prisoner Knows
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The injured man, Wren, confesses Crane believes the Provision can control the valley's water rights outright—drought or flood, whichever squeezes the townsfolk into selling. Wren also reveals Crane has the missing half of the map, bought from Coral's father's executor. Beat: betrayal upon betrayal; Coral realizes his father tried to protect the secret even in death.

chapters.title: Night on the Weir
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Trapped below a weir by rising water, the team waits out the night sharing stories about Coral's father. Coral hears, for the first time, why his father left the expedition: he'd touched the Provision once and felt what it wanted from him. Beat: understanding replacing resentment, almost.

chapters.title: The Drowned Bell Rings
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. At the sunken village of Lower Vell, the chapel bell rings underwater as the river surges—Crane has opened the upper sluices to flush the team out of the gorge. Teo saves the journal at the cost of his dive gear and nearly his life. Beat: the antagonist stops being abstract.

chapters.title: Ines Bargains
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Captured briefly by Crane's site manager, Ines trades a false route up the east fork to buy the team a day. She lies beautifully and hates herself for enjoying it. Beat: loyalty tested by temptation—she could sell them all and be rich.

chapters.title: Gorge of the Second Marker
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The false route works; the true path climbs the gorge to a marker only Coral's childhood handwriting can decode. Climbing alone above a drop, Coral admits aloud—to no one—that he doesn't want to do this without them. They hear. Beat: the loner asks for help and survives it.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They reach the spring cavern: a chamber where the Provision—a lens of black glass set in living rock—bends the water into slow spirals. His father's final pages are here, addressed to Coral by name: an apology, and a warning that the glass 'shows you everything you've ever wanted fixed.' Beat: awe and dread in equal measure.

chapters.title: Everything You Wanted Fixed
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Alone at the lens, Coral sees visions: his father alive, the estrangement undone, the valley green forever. He understands the corruption—it doesn't grant power, it makes you its custodian until you're hollow. He reaches for it anyway. Beat: the hero at his weakest, wanting the lie.

chapters.title: Crane Takes the Water
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Crane arrives with his crew, takes the Provision from Coral's frozen hands, and immediately demonstrates its power: the river drops, wells fail, the town's pressure becomes leverage. Wren defects to the team. Beat: power's corruption made visible within minutes of possession.

chapters.title: Downstream Flood
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. With the source dammed by Crane's engineers, meltwater backs up behind the cavern; Maren calculates the collapse will drown the valley unless the blockage fails naturally—which it won't while the Provision holds the flow. The team splits: some evacuate the town, some return to the cavern. Beat: duty versus love made literal geography.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Glass
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Climax. In the flooding cavern, Coral confronts Crane, who is gaunt and rapt, already owned by the lens. Coral cannot take it without becoming what Crane is—so he does what his father's journal implied: he gives it what it wants, offering his own memory of his father as the price, and shatters the lens against the bedrock. The river bursts free. Beat: sacrifice of the thing he wanted most.

chapters.title: Afterwater
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The valley floods shallow and survivable; Crane, empty-eyed, is led away; the town rebuilds around a river that runs free again. Coral stays—not because there's a mystery left, but because Maren needs a second pair of hands on the boat and Ines has catalogued his father's papers under both their names. Beat: grief settling into something livable.

chapters.title: Measured in Years
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. One year later, Coral leads the annual expedition upstream—not for treasure, but to teach three local kids the route his father mapped. At the sea cave, the tide covers the entrance as if it never opened. Coral lets it. Beat: the drifter chooses a home, and the miles finally become years.
